**Finding: MFN — compliant (preferred position met).**

The agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on Corio. Exhibit B (PRICING, REVENUE SHARING FEES) and Section 17 (PAYMENT TERMS) fix the licence, MarketSite.net access, maintenance, revenue-share and implementation amounts outright; Section 4 (Fees) adds only tax and audit mechanics. Nothing requires us to give Commerce One terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, nor to disclose or match third-party offers.

I confirmed absence rather than relying on the planner's hint: targeted searches for "most favored/favourable", "no less favorable", "best/lowest pricing", "right to match", "first refusal", "comparable terms", "similarly situated" and "exclusivity" all returned nothing, and I read every commercially adjacent provision — Section 4, Exhibit B pricing and revenue sharing, Section 17, Section 13 (Shared Resources, which merely applies Commerce One's standard fees to personnel we request) and Exhibit D (expressly non-binding sales and marketing cooperation). None creates a pricing-parity duty running against us.

No redline proposed: the preferred position is the absence of a Customer-side MFN, and an MFN in our favour is welcome but not required by the playbook.
